accepted.s:
With reference to the Logistics Ease Across Different States (LEADS), consider the following statements:
1. LEADS was launched in 2018.
2. It was modelled on the World Bank's Logistics Performance Index.
3. It currently operates under the National Logistics Policy, 2022.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: LEADS was launched in 2018, modelled on the World Bank's Logistics Performance Index, and operates under the National Logistics Policy, 2022.
accepted.tq: Use the statement-combination method and verify the launch year, model and policy linkage separately.
accepted.sec: Logistics rankings - LEADS rank of AP

accepted.s: In LEADS 2023, Andhra Pradesh was placed in which category among coastal States?
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh was classified as an 'Achiever' among coastal States in LEADS 2023.
accepted.tq: Directly identify the precise ranking category rather than confusing it with the categories of other States.
accepted.sec: Logistics rankings - LEADS rank of AP

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched in the LEADS 2025 top-performer classification?
accepted.x: In LEADS 2025, Tamil Nadu was the top performer among coastal States, Uttar Pradesh among landlocked States, Mizoram among North-Eastern States and Delhi among Union Territories.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure category-State pair and eliminate the swapped geographical classifications.
accepted.sec: Logistics rankings - LEADS rank of AP

accepted.s: The SEZ policy in India was announced in 2000 under which framework?
o: The Export Promotion Capital Goods Scheme
accepted.x: The SEZ policy was announced in 2000 under the EXIM Policy, also referred to as the Foreign Trade Policy framework.
accepted.tq: Use the policy-name discrimination technique to distinguish the original SEZ framework from later policies.
accepted.sec: SEZ Act 2005 - objectives, SEZ vs EOU, incentives  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Which one of the following is NOT an objective of the SEZ policy?
1. Generation of additional economic activity
2. Promotion of exports of goods and services
3. Promotion of domestic and foreign investment
4. Protection of domestic industries from all foreign competition
5. Generation of employment
6. Development of infrastructure
accepted.x: The objectives include additional economic activity, exports, domestic and foreign investment, employment and infrastructure. Protection from all foreign competition is not listed as an objective.
accepted.tq: Find the statement that introduces an absolute protectionist objective absent from the recognised SEZ objectives.
accepted.sec: SEZ Act 2005 - objectives, SEZ vs EOU, incentives  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
An SEZ may be set up by which of the following?
1. The Central Government
2. A State Government
3. Any person
4. Only a joint venture of the Central and State Governments
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: An SEZ may be established by the Centre, a State or any person, jointly or severally. It is not restricted to a joint venture of the two levels of government.
accepted.tq: The word 'only' signals a likely over-restriction; distinguish eligible promoters from a compulsory joint-venture requirement.
accepted.sec: SEZ Act 2005 - objectives, SEZ vs EOU, incentives  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Proposals for setting up Special Economic Zones are routed through the State Government to the:
accepted.x: SEZ proposals go through the State Government to the Board of Approval.
accepted.tq: Apply the 'who would do this job?' method to identify the authority handling SEZ approvals.
accepted.sec: SEZ Act 2005 - objectives, SEZ vs EOU, incentives  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Section 18 of the Special Economic Zones Act, 2005 provides for:
o: One dry port within every SEZ
One Export-Oriented Unit in each SEZ
One Free Trade Warehousing Zone in every district
One International Financial Services Centre in each SEZ
accepted.x: Section 18 permits one International Financial Services Centre (IFSC) per SEZ.
accepted.tq: Use article-or-section precision to distinguish the specific facility authorised by Section 18.
accepted.sec: SEZ Act 2005 - objectives, SEZ vs EOU, incentives  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the trade and tariff treatment of an SEZ?
o: It is treated as foreign territory only for income-tax purposes.
It is treated as domestic territory for all trade and tariff purposes.
It has no special customs or tariff treatment.
It is treated as foreign territory for trade and tariff purposes and follows a single-window system.
accepted.x: An SEZ is treated as foreign territory for trade and tariffs and operates through a single-window system.
accepted.tq: Test the precise legal treatment by separating trade-and-tariff status from other forms of taxation.
accepted.sec: SEZ Act 2005 - objectives, SEZ vs EOU, incentives  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding an SEZ and an EOU:
1. An SEZ is a demarcated enclave established under the SEZ Act, 2005.
2. An EOU is a single unit that may be located anywhere under the Foreign Trade Policy scheme.
3. An SEZ consists only of a single unit and does not involve a developer.
4. An EOU is necessarily a developer-led enclave with its own infrastructure.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: An SEZ is a demarcated enclave under the 2005 Act, while an EOU is a single unit located anywhere under the FTP scheme. The developer-plus-units structure and dedicated infrastructure are features of an SEZ, not an EOU.
accepted.tq: Split the comparison into legal basis, location and organisational structure before selecting the combination.
accepted.sec: SEZ Act 2005 - objectives, SEZ vs EOU, incentives  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly states the difference between an SEZ and an EOU?
o: An SEZ has a developer plus units with its own infrastructure, whereas an EOU is a unit only.
An SEZ is a unit located anywhere, whereas an EOU is a demarcated enclave.
Both are demarcated enclaves created under the SEZ Act, 2005.
Both are single units operating without dedicated infrastructure.
accepted.x: An SEZ comprises a developer and units with its own infrastructure. An EOU is a single unit located anywhere under the FTP scheme.
accepted.tq: Use the structural contrast—developer plus units versus unit only—to resolve the comparison.
accepted.sec: SEZ Act 2005 - objectives, SEZ vs EOU, incentives  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The SEZ tax holidays were phased out during which period?
accepted.x: SEZ tax holidays were phased out between 2017 and 2020.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the reform period from nearby three-year periods by focusing on the stated beginning and end years.
accepted.sec: SEZ Act 2005 - objectives, SEZ vs EOU, incentives  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: According to the stated recent assessment, how many SEZ units shut down in five years?
accepted.x: The reported number of SEZ units that shut down in five years was 466.
accepted.tq: Use exact-number discrimination; the close alternatives alter the digits rather than the underlying concept.
accepted.sec: SEZ Act 2005 - objectives, SEZ vs EOU, incentives  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Since April 2026, SEZ units have been permitted to sell goods in the domestic Indian market:
o: Without any customs or tariff conditions in all cases
Only after paying an additional export subsidy
Only through a Free Trade Warehousing Zone
accepted.x: Since April 2026, SEZ units may sell in India at concessional duty.
accepted.tq: Identify the precise incentive condition and reject absolute statements such as 'without any' conditions.
accepted.sec: SEZ Act 2005 - objectives, SEZ vs EOU, incentives  [other exams, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The proposal for a dry port at Sri City, in Tirupati district, is under review by the:
accepted.x: The Sri City dry port proposal in Tirupati district is under review by an Inter-Ministerial Committee.
accepted.tq: Match the project with the authority currently examining it; do not confuse it with the SEZ approval body.
accepted.sec: Export infrastructure - dry ports, ICDs, corridors  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The proposed dry port at Sri City is intended, among other things, to facilitate:
accepted.x: The Sri City dry port proposal is associated with on-site customs clearance.
accepted.tq: Infer the operational purpose of the infrastructure from the customs-clearance function of a dry port.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Under the CBIC guidelines mentioned in relation to new dry ports, which one of the following distance restrictions is correct?
o: They are generally not allowed within 50 km of either a seaport or an ICD.
They are generally not allowed within 200 km of a seaport or 100 km of an ICD.
They are generally not allowed within 500 km of a seaport or 250 km of an ICD.
They are generally not allowed within 100 km of a seaport or 200 km of an ICD.
accepted.x: New dry ports are generally not allowed within 200 km of a seaport or within 100 km of an Inland Container Depot.
accepted.tq: Keep the two distance thresholds attached to the correct facilities; the trap reverses the seaport and ICD figures.
accepted.sec: Export infrastructure - dry ports, ICDs, corridors  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Andhra Pradesh receives relaxation from the general dry-port distance guidelines because it is classified as a:
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh is classified as a Blue-zone State and receives relaxation for trade hubs that lack logistics.
accepted.tq: Use the exact zone label and distinguish it from a geographical description such as landlocked.
accepted.sec: Export infrastructure - dry ports, ICDs, corridors  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The relaxation for Andhra Pradesh as a Blue-zone State applies to:
o: All proposed dry ports without exception
Only SEZs located within 100 km of an ICD
Only coastal ports operated by the Navy
accepted.x: The relaxation is available for trade hubs that lack logistics; it is not an unconditional relaxation for every proposed dry port.
accepted.tq: Watch for the extreme word 'all' and select the limited condition attached to the relaxation.
accepted.sec: Export infrastructure - dry ports, ICDs, corridors  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding industrial corridors in Andhra Pradesh is correct?
o: VCIC is India's first landlocked industrial corridor and forms part of the HBIC.
HBIC is India's first coastal industrial corridor and forms part of the ECEC.
VCIC is India's first coastal industrial corridor and forms part of the ECEC.
CBIC is India's first coastal industrial corridor and has no node in Andhra Pradesh.
accepted.x: The Visakhapatnam-Chennai Industrial Corridor (VCIC) is India's first coastal industrial corridor and is part of the East Coast Economic Corridor (ECEC).
accepted.tq: Use the corridor-name and status pairing; similar abbreviations are deliberate confusable distractors.
accepted.sec: Export infrastructure - dry ports, ICDs, corridors  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The Krishnapatnam North Node under the CBIC covers approximately:
accepted.x: The Krishnapatnam North Node under the Chennai-Bengaluru Industrial Corridor covers 10,834 acres.
accepted.tq: Test exact area figures by comparing the middle digits and rejecting near-number distractors.
accepted.sec: Export infrastructure - dry ports, ICDs, corridors  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: VCIC — Visakhapatnam, Chittoor/Srikalahasti-Yerpedu and Kopparthy nodes
ECEC — Orvakal as its only Andhra Pradesh node
accepted.x: Orvakal is the node of HBIC. VCIC is part of the ECEC and has the listed Visakhapatnam, Chittoor/Srikalahasti-Yerpedu and Kopparthy nodes; the statement that ECEC has Orvakal as its only AP node is incorrect.
accepted.tq: Find the wrongly assigned corridor by separating the ECEC-linked VCIC from the HBIC Orvakal node.
accepted.sec: Export infrastructure - dry ports, ICDs, corridors  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is a major criticism associated with Andhra Pradesh's export-oriented aquaculture and industrial development?
o: Pharma City has reduced salinity in all coastal agricultural fields.
Industrial corridors have caused the complete disappearance of port-based trade.
Shrimp cultivation has converted all coastal soils into forests and eliminated water pollution.
Shrimp cultivation has salinised coastal soils and Pharma City effluents have polluted local water.
accepted.x: The shrimp boom has contributed to salinisation of coastal soils, while effluents from Pharma City have polluted local water.
accepted.tq: Select the option containing both linked environmental criticisms and reject absolute reversals.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: The stated strategy of Andhra Pradesh's economic development is best described as:
o: Coast-led and export-oriented, built on the Visakhapatnam-Chennai Industrial Corridor
Landlocked and centred exclusively on the Orvakal node
Agriculture-only and independent of port infrastructure
Inland and consumption-oriented, centred on Hyderabad's industrial clusters
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh follows a coast-led and export-oriented strategy built on the Visakhapatnam-Chennai Industrial Corridor, India's first coastal industrial corridor.
accepted.tq: Translate the combined geography and development facts into the most precise strategic description.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Why did Andhra Pradesh turn towards port-led development after bifurcation?
o: It acquired Hyderabad's industrial clusters and sought to decentralise them.
It lost Hyderabad's industrial clusters and therefore shifted towards port-led development.
It was prohibited from developing inland industries by the SEZ Act.
It became a landlocked State after bifurcation.
accepted.x: After bifurcation, Andhra Pradesh lost Hyderabad's industrial clusters and responded by pursuing port-led development.
accepted.tq: Trace the stated cause-and-effect relationship rather than confusing loss of clusters with a change in coastline.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: According to the comparative export data stated for 2024–25, Tamil Nadu's merchandise exports amounted to:
accepted.x: Tamil Nadu's merchandise exports were reported at $52.07 billion in 2024–25.
accepted.tq: Identify the exact export value while rejecting alternatives that change only the leading digit.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the comparative EPI ranking mentioned for Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh?
o: Both Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh 2nd
Both Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh 5th
accepted.x: Tamil Nadu ranks second in the Export Preparedness Index, while Andhra Pradesh ranks fifth.
accepted.tq: Check the direction of comparison carefully; the main trap reverses the ranks of the two States.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: The reported impact of the 50% United States tariff on Andhra Pradesh primarily concerned its:
accepted.x: The 50% US tariff was reported to have affected Andhra Pradesh's shrimp sector and aqua exports.
accepted.tq: Link the trade measure to the specific export sector rather than to unrelated industries.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: In the context of the reported impact of the 50% US tariff, which combination was cited by the Chief Minister as being at risk?
o: ₹25,000 crore of software exports and 2.5 lakh industrial workers
₹52,070 crore of merchandise exports and 5 lakh farm families
₹25,000 crore of aqua exports and 2.5 lakh farm families
₹2,500 crore of aqua exports and 25,000 farm families
accepted.x: The Chief Minister stated that about ₹25,000 crore of aqua exports and 2.5 lakh farm families were at risk.
accepted.tq: Read the paired magnitude carefully; both the rupee value and the number of families must be correct.
accepted.sec: Universal angles
